themes.theme_title: The Kitchen: Food Production and Processing Unit

topic_metadata.topic_title: The Kitchen: Food Production and Processing Unit

topics.core_competency: The learner designs and manages a kitchen that is safe, efficient and functional taking into account of the various elements.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: design the kitchen considering ventilation, illumination, materials and colour to ensure efficiency in work. (u, s, gs)
apply detergents appropriately for cleaning different surfaces in the kitchen. (u, s, v, gs)
purify water for use in the kitchen/food processing unit. (s, v, gs)
dispose of refuse appropriately to maintain hygiene in the kitchen/ food processing unit. (u, s, v, gs)
prevent and manage risks and hazards to ensure safety in the kitchen/food processing unit. (u, s, v, gs)
use and manage fuels safely and efficiently in the kitchen/food processing unit. (u, s, gs)

must_cover: kitchen plans: L-shaped, U-shaped, island, and galley layouts
kitchen work triangle (sink, stove, and refrigerator)
ventilation, illumination, and colour coordination
counters, lighting equipment, storage
detergents: classification, choice and use
water purification methods
refuse disposal: liquid and solid
drainage systems: surface, subsurface, slope, French drains, gutter systems
safety measures/practices in the kitchen
fire extinguishers: design, use and operating principles
fuels: renewable and non-renewable, solid and gas

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to: i) design kitchen plans, such as L-shaped, U-shaped, island, and galley layouts, with a strong emphasis on the kitchen work triangle (sink, stove, and refrigerator); and ii) sketch and plan a kitchen layout—learners will design a kitchen considering ventilation, illumination, and colour coordination to enhance efficiency.
Learners present their sketches and explain how their design optimises work efficiency as they take note of important points.

Learners analyse the use of elements such as counters, ventilation, lighting equipment, colour and storage, considering their functionality and effectiveness for kitchen use as they take note of important points.
Learners investigate and document how materials used in counter tops and flooring contribute to durability and ease of maintenance of a kitchen as they take notes.

In small groups, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to: i) discuss the classification, choice and use of detergents in cleaning surfaces of the kitchen/food processing unit as they take notes
demonstrate the use and cleaning action of modern and locally obtained detergents in the kitchen as they take notes.

In small groups, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to: i) brainstorm and record the need for purifying water in the kitchen/food processing unit; various ways in which water gets contaminated
carry out processes of purifying water as they note the important points

In pairs, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to: i) discuss the treatment of refuse (liquid and solid refuse); ii) analyse the different types of drainage systems, including surface, subsurface, slope, French drains, and gutter systems, and describe the specific maintenance practices required for each
sensitise the community about proper refuse disposal and safety measures in the kitchen, environmental impact and sustainability.

In groups, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to: i) discuss essential safety measures/practices in the kitchen to prevent accidents and manage risks effectively; ii) analyse the design, use and operating principles of tools and material used in managing hazards (e.g., fire extinguishers); and iii) apply essential safety measures/practices in the kitchen to prevent accidents and manage risks effectively as they take note of important points.

In small groups, learners use textbooks, ICT resources, and additional resources to: i) classify the different types of fuels (renewable and non-renewable); ii) analyse the advantages and disadvantages of the different fuels in the kitchen
produce different types of fuels (solid and gas) to use in the kitchen
demonstrate the use of various equipment that use different fuels.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage with learners as they discuss and judge their understanding of the work triangle as they come up with the different efficient kitchen designs and layouts.
Observe learners as they develop plans and look out for their ability to use imaginations to explore possibilities of developing different kitchen plans.

Evaluate the different kitchen designs and write-ups for accuracy of information about the: i) types, properties and maintenance of materials used in counter tops and flooring, and ii) correct positioning of the key elements in the kitchen designs (ventilation, lighting, equipment, colour and storage.
Converse with learners as they demonstrate the cleaning action of both modern and local detergents to evaluate the correct use and effectiveness of each type of detergent.
Observe learners as they present, look out for their ability to talk confidently and explain ideas when classifying and using detergents.
Evaluate the demonstration to ensure that the steps and procedures used are appropriate, efficient, and aligned with best practices for using both modern and traditional detergents.
Dialogue with learners to evaluate their understanding of the different ways in which water can be purified and how they correctly apply different methods of water purification.
Observe learners as they purify water using different methods, and look out for effective interaction with others.
Evaluate the purified water for colour, taste and smell.
Converse with learners to establish their understanding of the correct refuse disposal and the risks associated with wrong disposal.
Observe learners as they sensitise communities, and look out for their ability to communicate effectively.
Evaluate their write-ups for accuracy of information on the treatment process and essential safety measures/ practices in the kitchen.
Engage with the learners during the discussion to gauge their understanding of the prevention and management of risks /hazards in the kitchen.
Observe learners as they demonstrate application of safety measures /practices to prevent risks/hazards.
Evaluate the demonstration to ensure that the steps and procedures used are appropriate, efficient, and aligned with best practices of risk and hazard management.
Converse with learners to appraise their understanding of different fuels, and ways of transforming raw materials into usable fuels.
Observe them as they follow correct procedures to produce and use different fuels. Look out for their ability to use imaginations to explore possibilities as they produce different fuels.
Evaluate the fuels produced and look out for usability, functionality, and cost-effectiveness.

topics.core_competency: The learner develops appropriate diet plans to prevent and manage nutritional imbalances for the health of an individual, family and the community.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the chemistry of proteins in relation to their biological functions. (u, s, gs)
evaluate the quality of protein in preventing and managing protein imbalances in individuals, family and community. (u, gs)
examine the chemistry of carbohydrates in relation to their biological functions. (u, s, gs)
analyse the importance of fibre in maintaining a healthy diet and preventing chronic diseases for good nutrition, health and overall well-being.
manage the effects of carbohydrate imbalances in the body. (u, s, gs)

must_cover: Proteins: chemical composition (amino acid, peptide bonds, polypeptide chains)
Classification of amino acids and proteins
Protein quality: biological value, supplementation value, net protein utilisation, protein efficiency ratio
Protein imbalances: moderate acute malnutrition (MAM), severe acute malnutrition (SAM)
Carbohydrates: chemical composition (glucose, fructose, galactose; glycosidic bonds; disaccharide, oligosaccharide, polysaccharides)
Types of polysaccharides: starch, cellulose, glycogen, chitin
Fibre: classification, food sources, role in disease prevention
Carbohydrate imbalances: overweight, obesity, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, anorexia nervosa, dental caries

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small groups, learners use ICT resources and textbooks to: i) investigate the chemical composition—building blocks (amino acid, peptide bonds and polypeptide chains) and structure of proteins
discuss the classification of amino acids and proteins; explore the physical and chemical properties of proteins, relate them to their biological functions

In pairs, learners use ICT resources and textbooks to: i) discuss the concept of protein quality, (biological value, supplementation value, net protein utilisation, protein efficiency ratio) , methods of assessing protein quality and classification of proteins
explore the adequacy of protein intake in relation to the needs of individuals and take note of the important points
brainstorm the health effects of protein imbalances in the body (moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) and severe acute malnutrition (SAM)
evaluate the management strategies for protein imbalances in the body; develop recipes for dishes to manage protein imbalances
Learners prepare one of the dishes developed to manage protein imbalance as they take note of important points.

In small learning clusters, learners use ICT resources and textbooks to: i) discuss the chemical composition —building blocks (glucose, fructose and galactose; glycosidic bonds and disaccharide, oligosaccharide and polysaccharides (types of polysaccharides e.g., starch, cellulose glycogen chitin), and classification of carbohydrates
explore the physical and chemical properties of carbohydrates and relate them to their biological functions

In small learning clusters, learners use ICT and textbooks to: i) examine the classification and food sources of fibre; ii) discuss the role of fibre in relation to its health benefits in disease prevention

In pairs, learners work on a project to: i) examine the various fibre imbalances (e.g., constipation, diverticulitis, haemorrhoids, rectal and anal cancer); ii) modify a recipe of any common dish to make it fibre rich; iii) prepare the dish rich in fibre; iv) formulate sensitisation messages; and v) visit a community (school, church or village) and sensitise them on prevention of fibre imbalance.
brainstorm the impact of carbohydrate imbalances in the body, (overweight and obesity, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, anorexia nervosa, and dental caries)
develop dishes to manage carbohydrate imbalances; prepare one of the dishes developed to manage carbohydrate imbalance

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Dialogue with learners as they discuss and evaluate how they relate the chemistry of proteins to their biological functions.
Observe learners as they sort and analyse information on composition, structure and biological functions of proteins.
Appraise their write-ups for accuracy of the composition, structure and biological functions of proteins.
Engage with learners during the discussion and appraise their ability to relate protein quality to management of protein imbalances in the body.
Observe learners for the ability to evaluate different solutions as they develop dishes to manage protein imbalances.
Judge the dish prepared to manage protein imbalances for suitability, appearance, taste and correct serving portions.
Dialogue with learners as they discuss and evaluate how they relate the chemistry of carbohydrates to their biological functions
Observe learners as they sort and analyse information on composition, structure and biological functions of carbohydrates.
Critique their write-ups for accuracy of the composition, structure and biological functions of carbohydrates.

Engage learners as they examine the classification and food sources of fibre and look out for: i) clear distinction between the classes, food sources of each category; and ii) accurate responses on the role of fibre in the diet.

Observe learners as they modify recipes to make fibre rich dishes and judge their ability to: i) sort and analyse information to predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions; and ii) take responsibility for their own learning.

Appraise: i) the modified fibre dishes for suitability, acceptability, creativity, taste and appearance; and ii) sensitisation session for communication skills, correctness of the messages, social responsibility and harmony.
Converse with learners as they brainstorm and establish their understanding of how the carbohydrate imbalances come about and their impact on health.
Observe learners and look out for their ability to work with others to generate ideas as they prepare one of the dishes to manage carbohydrate imbalance.
Critique the dish prepared to manage carbohydrate imbalances for suitability, appearance, taste and correct serving portions.

topics.core_competency: The learner develops appropriate diet plans to prevent and manage nutritional imbalances for the health of an individual, family and the community.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the chemistry of lipids in relation to their biological functions. (u, gs)
apply the properties of lipids to their use in food production. (u, s, gs)
manage lipid imbalances in the body. (s, v, gs)
apply the knowledge of food processing to produce lipids for home use. (u, s, v, gs)
analyse vitamins and apply the knowledge to promote nutrition, health and disease prevention. (u, s, v, gs)
manage vitamin imbalances in the body. (u, s, v, gs)
explore mineral elements and apply the knowledge to promote nutrition, health and disease prevention. (u, s, v, gs)
manage mineral element imbalances in the body. (u, s, v, gs)
appreciate the essential role of water in maintaining overall health and well-being. (u, v, gs)

must_cover: Lipids: chemical composition (fatty acids, glycerol), structure (triglyceride, ester bonds, condensation, hydrocarbon chains)
Lipid imbalances: hyperlipidaemia, cholesterolemia, steatorrhoea
Lipid extraction sources: avocado, simsim, peanut, sunflower, shearnut
Vitamins: classification (fat-soluble, water-soluble), sources, functions, properties (solubility, sensitivity)
Vitamin imbalances: deficiencies and toxicity
Minerals: macro-minerals (calcium, potassium), trace elements (iron, zinc)
Mineral absorption: factors affecting stability and bioavailability
Water: properties, distribution in body, effects of dehydration, water and electrolyte balance (acid-base buffer system)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small learning clusters, learners use ICT resources and textbooks to: i) discuss the chemical composition—building blocks (fatty acids and glycerol), formation of a lipid (triglyceride), ester bonds, condensation, hydrocarbon chains; and classification of lipids
explore the physical and chemical properties of lipids and relate them to their biological functions and culinary uses
create dishes to show healthy use of lipids in cookery and write the recipes; use the recipes and prepare the dishes created
performs basic nutritional status assessments (body mass index (BMI), mid upper arm circumference (MUAC), waist to hip ratio etc)
formulates a recipe for a dish to manage lipid imbalances; prepares a dish using the formulated recipe

identify the suitable food sources (e.g., avocado, simsim, peanut, sunflower, shearnut) for lipid extraction; develop a procedure for extracting lipids from food sources; and extract the oil, pack, label and market the product
categorise vitamins — (fat-soluble and water-soluble, giving examples) and identify sources of each of the vitamins
analyse the properties (solubility, sensitivity to light, heat, and pH changes) and functions of each vitamin
identify vitamin imbalances (deficiencies and toxicity) among individuals
formulate recipes for dishes to manage vitamin imbalances; and prepare a dish using the formulated recipe
categorise mineral elements (e.g., macro-minerals like calcium, potassium, or trace elements like iron, zinc) and identify sources of each of the mineral elements
analyse functions of each mineral elements, absorption process in the body, storage sites and factors affecting absorption (e.g., diet, inhibitors, enhancers)

In small groups, learners use ICT resources, textbooks and any other material to: i) examine water (sources, proportion) and its distribution within different compartments of the body and how it affects overall health (hydration, the functioning of organs and systems).
explore and document the effects of dehydration on body functions; explain the mechanisms of water and electrolyte balance in the human body (acid-base buffer system)

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Converse with learners as they present their findings and look out for their understanding of the structure of the different types of lipids.
Observe learners during presentation and judge their ability to sort and analyse information on the structure of lipids.
Observe learners demonstrate the culinary uses of lipids and check their ability to plan and carryout investigations on the use of lipids in cookery.

Converse with learners as they perform the nutritional assessment and formulate the recipes and judge: i) their ability to take accurate measurements; and ii) appropriateness of the recipes in managing lipid imbalances.
Evaluate the dish (product) for: texture, colour, taste, flavour and suitability in the management of lipid imbalances.
Observe learners as they plan and extract oil form foods and look out for identification of problems and ways forward.
Evaluate the extracted oil (product) for consistency, flavour, colour, choice of packaging materials, package, label and cost.

Converse with learners to evaluate their understanding of: i) categories of vitamins; ii) function of vitamins in the body; and iii) factors affecting solubility, stability, bio-availability of vitamins.
Converse with learners to evaluate their ability to identify vitamin imbalances and formulate recipes to manage the imbalances.
Observe learners as they prepare dishes to manage vitamin imbalances and look out for their ability to measure ingredients accurately.

Converse with learners as they discuss and judge their ability to: i) categorise and analyse sources and functions of mineral elements; and ii) explain the absorption and interactions with other nutrients.
Observe learners as they formulate recipes and prepare the dishes and judge their skills of problem solving, creativity and innovation.
Converse with learners as they discuss and appraise their ability to relate how properties of water contribute to its vital roles in biological processes in the body.
Appraise the write-ups for correct information on: i) properties and functions of water; ii) effects of dehydration; and iii) mechanism of water and electrolyte balance.

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Duration: 100 Periods (Total for Topic 2, split between Term 1 and Term 2)

topic_metadata.topic_title: Heat and Thermodynamics in Food Production

topics.core_competency: The learner applies heat and thermodynamics principles to manage cooking processes, optimises energy use, and controls temperatures for efficient kitchen operations.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: apply the knowledge of expansion in states of matter to food production operations. (u, s, gs)
apply the knowledge of phase changes in the various food production processes and technologies. (u, s, v, gs)
apply the knowledge of thermodynamics in operations of the food production unit. (u, s, v, gs)

must_cover: Expansion in solids: thermostats in appliances
Expansion in liquids: anomalous expansion of water
Expansion in gases: leavening agents, heat distribution in ovens
Bimetallic strip applications: room heaters, cookers, fire alarms, timers
Phase changes: melting, cooling, evaporation, boiling, condensation, distillation, humidity, damp
Heat transfer: solids, liquids, gases
Heat capacity, latent heat, latent heat of vapourisation, latent heat of fusion

suggested_learning_activities.description: examine the principles and applications of expansion in solids, liquids and gases in food production
demonstrate thermal expansion in metals (e.g., covers of jars, applying heat loosens tight metal; place a hot pan in cold water and observe contraction of screws or rivets)
illustrate how a bimetallic strip is used in the operation of room heaters, cookers, fire alarms and timers
differentiate between the following: i) melting and cooling; ii) evaporation and boiling; iii) condensation and distillation; and iv) humidity and damp.
discuss the application of the different phase changes, and application of humidity and damp.
examine the modes of heat transfer in solids, liquids, gases and their applications in the kitchen
analyse the concepts of heat capacity, latent heat and their applications in the food production and processing operations.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Dialogue with learners as they demonstrate expansion in solids, liquids and gases and evaluate their understanding of the principles involved.
Evaluate the demonstrations done for appropriate use of equipment, correct procedures and results.
Ask targeted questions to learners to gauge their comprehension on concepts such as melting, boiling, evaporation, cooling, condensation and distillation in daily operations of the kitchen.
Appraise the write up for appropriate applications of the different concepts in the kitchen.
Converse with learners as they examine the modes of heat transfer to evaluate their ability to apply these principles in cooking.
Appraise the write-ups for the correct applications of thermodynamics in the food production unit.

topics.core_competency: The learner develops an understanding of nutrient absorption and metabolism and applies this knowledge to promote health, manage diet, and enhance overall well-being.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: apply the knowledge of nutrient absorption and metabolism in management of meals. (u, gs)
relate the energy and other nutrient requirements with recommended dietary allowances (RDA) to make informed dietary choices. (u, s, gs)

must_cover: Nutrient absorption: transport, bloodstream uptake, factors affecting absorption

Catabolism and anabolism: proteins (deamination, transamination, carnitine cycle), carbohydrates (glycolysis, Kreb's cycle, glycogenesis, gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, electron transport chain), lipids (lipolysis, lipogenesis, cholesterol synthesis, ketosis)
Energy production: roles of different nutrients
Recommended Dietary Allowances (RDA) for various age groups
Food tables: nutrient composition calculation

suggested_learning_activities.description: analyse how nutrients from food are transported, and taken up into the bloodstream.
study the processes and factors that affect nutrient absorption (factors that hinder or enhance absorption) of each nutrient.

examine catabolism and anabolism of the following nutrients within cells: i) proteins (deamination, transamination, carnitine cycle); ii) carbohydrates (glycolysis and Kreb’s cycle, glycogenesis, gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, electron transport chain and the hormones influencing them); and iii) lipids—(lipolysis and lipogenesis, cholesterol synthesis, ketosis hormones influencing them)
assess the energy and other nutrient requirements for various age groups and take note of important points
use food tables to identify the nutrient composition of different foodstuffs, and calculate the nutrient requirements for different categories of people
evaluate the recommended dietary allowances (RDAs) for different categories of people to ensure that their diets are nutritionally adequate

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Conduct a reflective conversation with learners as they present their findings about nutrient absorption, catabolism and anabolism in the body and focus on their ability to come up with factors that affect these processes.
Observe learners as they present to evaluate their ability to chronologically describe the nutrient absorption and metabolic process and how they work effectively in diverse teams.
Appraise the plenary presentation focusing on accuracy and coherence of information on nutrient absorption and metabolism in the body and the factors that affect the processes.
Converse with learners during the discussion to justify their understanding of energy requirements in the body and the factors that influence energy needs.
Observe learners during plenary and judge their ability to use and comprehend the food tables effectively.
Appraise the write-ups for accuracy of information on assessment of energy requirements, use of food tables and RDAs of different categories of people.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Scientific Principles and their Applications in Food Production

topics.core_competency: The learner optimises the use of scientific principles and applications for efficient operations to promote sustainability and safety in the food production unit.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: apply the concepts of matter to improve the operation techniques in the food industry. (u, s, gs)
apply various types of forces in the operation of kitchen appliances to improve efficiency. (u, s, gs)
analyse the application of pressure in specific kitchen tasks and appliances to ensure efficiency. (u, s, v, gs)
apply the knowledge of electric current in the operation of the food production unit. (u, s, v, gs)
analyse the process of oxidation and reduction in food production. (u, s, v, gs)
apply the concept of oxidation and reduction in daily life. (u, s, v, gs)
apply the concept of pH and pH modifications. (u, s, v, gs)

must_cover: Concepts of matter: density, absorption, capillarity, osmosis, surface tension, adsorption, solubility, elasticity
Impact of materials (plastics, metals) on environment and health
Forces in kitchen tasks: Centrifugal & centripetal, friction, gravity, normal force, magnetic force
Simple machines: lever, pulleys, wedges, screws, weighing equipment, wheel and axle, inclined planes
Pressure in kitchen tasks: pressure cooker, coffee makers, knives, rolling pins
Electric current: current, voltage, resistance, power, heating effect
Electrical safety: insulators, fuses, circuit breakers, earthing, colour coding sockets
Simple electric repairs: replacing fuse, lamp holders, sockets, wiring three pin plugs
Oxidation and reduction: Maillard's reaction, food preservation, fermentation, colour development
Reducing agents: ascorbic acid, antioxidants
pH measurements: food, beverages, cleaning agents
pH modifications: acids and bases, neutral products

suggested_learning_activities.description: discuss how density, absorption, capillarity, osmosis, surface tension, adsorption, solubility and elasticity affect the texture, consistency and quality of consumer products (bread, cakes and salad dressings).
evaluate the environmental and health impacts of using certain materials (such as plastics and metals) based on their physical and chemical properties
analyse the effect of different forces in carrying out various kitchen tasks (Centrifugal & centripetal, friction, gravity, normal force, magnetic force)
apply the knowledge about the relationship between mechanical advantage, velocity ratio and efficiency in the selection of equipment in the food production unit
discover the types and applications of simple machines (lever, pulleys, wedges, screws, weighing equipment, wheel and axle, inclined planes
evaluate the design and functionality of kitchen appliances that use pressure (pressure cooker, coffee makers, knives or rolling pins)
explain the relationship between pressure, force, and surface area of kitchen tools
examine the relationship between current, voltage, resistance and power in electrical circuits and calculate power used by electric and gas appliances
demonstrate simple electric repairs in the food production unit (replacing fuse, lamp holders, sockets, wiring three pin plugs)
investigate the oxidation and reduction reactions in food production processes/unit

demonstrate the use of oxidation and reduction reactions to either take advantage or prevent the negative effects (Maillard’s reaction, food preservation, fermentation, colour development) in food production
measure the pH of various kitchen or household items and show how changes in pH impact chemical reactions (baking or fermentation)

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Converse with learners as they discuss the concepts of density, absorption, capillarity, osmosis, surface tension, adsorption, solubility and elasticity and appraise their ability to identify how they affect quality of some common consumer products.
Evaluate the experiments carried out and appraise the correctness of procedures and results.
Converse with learners during the discussions to judge their ability to apply/use/categorise the different forces involved in kitchen tasks.
Evaluate the write-ups for clear analysis of: i) the effects of forces; ii) the explanation of the relations; and iii) the correct applications of simple machines.

Converse with learners as they share on: the different types of pressure and their applications in kitchen tasks and as they design an operation mechanism of kitchen appliances which relies on the pressure principle.

Evaluate the write-ups for clarity of the different types of pressure and their applications in kitchen tasks and correct design and operation mechanism of kitchen appliances which relies on the pressure principle.
Converse with learners as they discuss to justify the application of the heating effect of electric current.
Evaluate the products of the simple repairs for correct wiring and placements of components.
Converse with learners as they discuss and evaluate their ability to recommend good practices during food preparation and storage.
Evaluate the product for effectiveness of different methods for preventing or controlling oxidation in food in the kitchen.
Converse with learners to establish the role of reduction reactions, reducing agents and their influence on food properties
Evaluate the product of reduction reactions and appraise for colour changes, nutrient loss prevention and prevention of spoilage.
Converse with learners to judge their ability to explain the role of pH measurements and pH modifications in food operations and household cleaning activities.
Evaluate the write-ups and end product of the modifications on pH measurements of substances for accuracy.

topics.core_competency: The learner justifies the importance of various additives, evaluates their safety and applies them to produce variety in organoleptic properties, nutritional value and shelf life of foods.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: appreciate food additives as used in food production to improve quality. (u, s, v, gs)
evaluate the potential health effects of using various food additives. (u, s, v, gs)

must_cover: Food additives: classification, nutritive value, roles
Information/labels and instructions for use
Health effects: positive and negative
Strategies to minimise negative health effects

suggested_learning_activities.description: search and document information on food additives to identify their classification, nutritive value and roles in food production
create a brochure or poster for their findings and share in plenary
collect different empty packages (with labels) of different food additives and stick them on charts to be displayed for a gallery walk.

prepare and compare two similar dishes; one cooked with different food additives while the other cooked without. (For example, bake cake with different flavours and spices versus a plain one or cake with preservatives versus one without)
observe and document the differences in taste, texture, appearance, and shelf life of the products above over a set period of time
search and document information on seasonings, flavourings and food additives and identify their potential health effects (both positive or negative
discuss strategies to minimise or prevent the negative health effects of food additives.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Converse with learners as they discuss, and appraise their understanding of the classes, roles and instructions for use of additives in food production.
Evaluate the products from the modified recipes to establish the variations in taste, colour, texture and shelf life.
Converse with learners as they discuss to measure their strategies to minimise or prevent the negative health effects of food additives.
Evaluate the write-ups for appropriate suggestions of the strategies to minimise or prevent the negative health effects of seasonings, flavourings and food additives.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Planning and Preparation of Meals (Part I)

topics.core_competency: The learner plans and prepares balanced meals efficiently, while considering dietary needs to promote health and minimise wastage of resources.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore the values of foods in order to make informed food choices for diets of different categories of people. (u, gs)
prepare, cook and serve egg, milk and cheese dishes as part of a meal to suit the dietary needs of different categories of people. (u, s, v, gs)
plan meals to suit different categories of people. (u, s, v, gs)
appreciate traditional dishes and prepare them as part of meals for different categories of people. (u, s, v, gs)

must_cover: Values of foods: nutritive, economic, dietetic, culinary
Foods: milk and milk products, meat, fish, poultry, offals, eggs, cereals, pulses, nuts, fruits, vegetables, textured vegetable protein, roots, tubers, plantain
Meal planning considerations: "eat well guide", "my plate", special groups (invalids, convalescents, vegetarians, allergies)
Traditional dishes: factors influencing choice (culture, social, economic, globalisation)

suggested_learning_activities.description: analyse and document the nutritive, economic, dietetic and culinary value of: i) milk and milk products; ii) meat, fish and poultry iii) offals; iv) eggs; v) cereals, pulses and nuts; vi) fruits and vegetables; vii) textured vegetable protein; viii) roots, tubers and plantain; and ix) products of each of the named foods.
formulate recipes using foods, eggs, milk and cheese; and prepare, cook and serve eggs, milk and cheese dishes to suit needs of different people.

Discuss the concept of “eat well guide” and design their own “my plate”; examine the factors considered when planning meals for the different categories of people; plan meals for different categories of people taking into account their needs

examine factors and behaviours that influence the choice and use of traditional dishes in meals (dietary behaviours, eating habits, cultural and social influence, health and nutritional trends and accessibility, influence of globalisation, economic factors)
plan, prepare, cook and serve traditional dishes from different regions; plan, prepare and cook suitable accompaniments to be served with the traditional dishes

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Probe learners during the discussions to judge their understanding of the concepts of nutritive, dietetic, culinary and economic values of foods and how they are used to make a balanced diet.
Appraise the write-ups and look out for clarity of information on the nutritive, dietetic, culinary and economic values of different foods.
Engage learners in a discussion while developing and testing recipes to evaluate if the formulated recipes meet the needs of the people being planned for.
Appraise the prepared dishes for taste, colour, texture, readiness, appropriateness and presentation of the dishes.
Dialogue with learners as they plan meals to judge their understanding of the key considerations of meals for different categories of people.
Evaluate the meal plans for nutritional balance, variety in texture and colour.
Converse with learners to evaluate their understanding of the factors that influence the use of traditional dishes in meals.
Critique the dishes basing on these parameters: taste, colour, texture, readiness and presentation.

topics.core_competency: The learner explores various types of beverages, and incorporates them appropriately in the diet for health and wellbeing.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse beverages as used in the diet to promote wellbeing. (u, s, gs)
prepare beverages as part of a meal. (u, s, v, gs)

must_cover: Classification of beverages
Value in diet
Benefits and drawbacks
Preparation: hot and cold, fermented, non-alcoholic

suggested_learning_activities.description: assess the classification of beverages and their value in the diet
examine the benefits and drawbacks of the different beverages as they take note of the findings
formulate recipes for modified healthier beverages to be prepared as part of the meal and take note of the modifications
prepare hot and cold fermented, non- alcoholic beverages

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Converse with learners and critique their ability to distinguish the benefits and drawbacks of beverages.
